Take the Plunge is the first episode of the first season of Battle for Dream Island created by twin brothers Cary and Michael Huang, and was released into two separate parts. It was released on New Year's Day 2010, and set up the basic format of modern object shows.
Plot
On the fictional continent of Goiky, twenty anthropomorphic objects--Pencil, Match, Flower, Ice Cube, Bubble, Pin, Blocky, Needle, Woody, Teardrop, Leafy, Tennis Ball, Snowball, Rocky, Eraser, Pen, Spongy, Firey, Coiny and Golf Ball--are interacting with each other in a grassland. A dark gray speaker box called the Announcer descends from the sky and announces the existence of Dream Island, an island designed to be the ultimate paradise, and that whoever owns the island can decide who is allowed onto it. He starts a contest for the island with the twenty objects as contestants.
The first challenge is to see who can stay on a balance beam the longest. Two of the objects, Pin and Leafy, win the first contest and get to organize the teams of the competition; the Squishy Cherries and the Squashy Grapes. The second contest is a race to make a boat and row it to the finish line across the Goiky Canal, which the Squishy Cherries win.
History
Production and release
In 2009, the twins started production on Battle for Dream Island at the age of 12, releasing the episode on January 1, 2010. The episode, alongside other future episodes, were animated using Adobe Flash.
Reception
/Film writer Witney Seibold called the series an "underground phenomenon", citing a lack of coverage by the media and the absence of a Wikipedia article despite its popularity, while noting its "sweet, direct, Kindergarten appeal". Russ Burlingame of ComicsBeat praised the series's avoidance of "predictable traits" and "lazy jokes".
